messages:
olivia: Heads up — pushed the rebuilt CUDA 12 base images to our registry at 03:10 UTC and started a canary rollout to us-west-2 nodes. Immediately seeing node flapping and GPU driver module reloads on ~12% of nodes in the pool. Autoscaler started reclaiming pods. Rolling back the image now.

sam: Which image tag exactly? Did the driver package change on the host or only the container toolchain?

olivia: Image tag: redwood/cuda-base:12.1-toolchain-gcc13-20260310. Only container toolchain changed (gcc13, new glibc build), but a few nodes reported kernel oops referencing nvidia. Suspect userspace/driver ABI mismatch.

rene: Do we have a minimal repro? Canary job logs?

olivia: Captured the pod logs and kernel dmesg on affected nodes. Short snippets: 
```
Kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:03:00): 31, pid=14237, GPU has fallen off the bus
container: runtime error: cudart reported CUDA driver version mismatch
nvidia-smi: Failed to initialize NVML: Driver/library version mismatch
```

infra-bot: [alert] us-west-2 GPU pool available_gpus dropped from 480 -> 421 (03:22 UTC). Scheduled scale-up queued.

li: Looks like the container was built against a newer libcuda (from the toolkit) and the host driver (525.x) can't match the driver's expected ABI. Did the image include a vendor-provided libcuda by accident?

olivia: No vendor libs intentionally included, but the rebuild stage used the system-provided lib from the CUDA toolkit image during multi-stage build. So libcuda ended up in the final image. Bad.

sam: That explains the "Driver/library version mismatch" from nvidia-smi. Two mitigations: 1) strip vendor libcuda from final image, 2) pin toolchain to gcc11 for now to avoid other subtle ABI issues while we rebuild.

emily: Impact on prod metrics: p99 inference latency +12% for routes backed by the affected pool; retry rate up ~3% (retries translate to ~8% extra GPU time, so cost spike). Not great.

marco: Proposed rollout plan: 
1) Immediately revert registry tag for us-west and eu-west canaries to :cuda-11-stable.
2) Create a dedicated "cuda12-canary" worker set with drained nodes and updated drivers (525 -> 535) to test the new images end-to-end.
3) For container rebuilds, add a final image step to verify no /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcuda.so is included and run `nvidia-smi` inside an ephemeral container against host driver.

rene: Also add a linter to the image CI that fails the build if it includes libcuda or libnvidia-*. The "copy from toolkit" pattern is a known footgun.

olivia: Agreed. For the immediate rollback I'm unpublishing the 12.1-toolchain-* tags and triggering redeploy to the older :cuda-11 images. Starting that now.

li: One more datapoint — some nodes reported NCCL collectives timing out with errors like: `NCCL WARN Call to connect() failed, errno 113` after the driver mismatch. That caused gRPC retries and exacerbated the latency. Might be that the driver reload killed some processes mid-collective.

sam: If driver reloads were frequent, we should consider tainting nodes where driver-version != desired and kill long-running GPU workloads until fixed. We can add a kube-probe that checks `cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version` and marks not-ready on mismatch.

emily: Ops question — what's the cost/ops overhead for keeping a separate driver-upgrade pool per region? Could we just do a rolling driver upgrade per AZ instead of full fleet?

marco: Rolling per-AZ is fine and cheaper. We should: cordon AZ, upgrade drivers on the node image, run 3-day soak with real traffic (canary traffic routed), then uncordon. That avoids full-fleet outages. Reserve small burst capacity in other AZs during the upgrade to handle failover costs.

rene: Action items I'm taking: add image CI check (no libcuda), add kube-probe for driver version mismatch, create a runbook for driver/toolkit upgrades.

olivia: I'm starting the rollback now and will kick off a rebuild pipeline that uses GCC=11 and explicitly strips toolkit libs from the final stage. Rebuild command I'm running: 
```
DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 docker build --build-arg GCC_VERSION=11 \
  --target runtime -t redwood/cuda-base:12.1-gcc11-20260310 .
# verify inside container:
ldd /usr/local/bin/some-binary | grep nvidia || true
nvidia-smi --query -x || true
```

infra-bot: [info] rollback of :12.1-toolchain-gcc13 initiated (03:38 UTC).

olivia: Will post follow-ups after the rebuild completes and initial canary runs. If anyone has spare cycles, can you help validate the runtime strip step? Ping me or @rene. :thumbsup:

marco: Also adding a short advisory to the infra calendar to avoid simultaneous driver upgrades + container toolchain swaps. Two moving pieces at once is how we fell into this.

sam: Good catch. Thanks for the fast rollback.

olivia: ETA for new images ~3h, canary soak 6-12h after that. I'll update thread when canary is green.
